title: Arnis
summary: Arnis is the stick art of the Philippines. In sport sparring two players in padding use light rattan sticks, exchanging numbered strikes, checks and a trap that takes the other stick away, scoring touches by skill and never by force.
howToPlay: Watch the rival's stance: it shows the move coming.
Tap the answering move while the marker is inside the bright zone.
A disarm only works once the rival is off balance.
rules: Every move beats two others and is beaten by two others; learn the circle.
Timing decides the strength of a move: inside the bright zone is full strength.
Strikes, weaves and checks score a touch; a trap and disarm scores two.
A round ends when one player is five points ahead, or when the clock runs out.
Tired players move weakly: use Breathe to recover.
heritageNote: Arnis, also called eskrima or kali, is taught across the Philippine islands with rattan sticks. Students learn numbered angles of attack and partner drills such as the double-stick weave before they ever spar, and it is now a school sport and a national martial art.
